name: cc.checkleaked/checkleaked-mcp
title: CheckLeaked
description: Search breach databases, crack hashes, run OSINT lookups, and monitor accounts via CheckLeaked.cc.

tools.name: checkleaked_site_faq
tools.description: Answers from the CheckLeaked.cc FAQ (how searches work, payments, API keys, accounts, privacy), best keyword matches first, at most 8. Use for questions about the service itself; for prices use checkleaked_site_plans. No API key, no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_site_plans
tools.description: Current CheckLeaked.cc plans: price in USD, duration in days, lookups per day, tracking slots and the search types each plan unlocks. Use to tell a user which plan a search type or volume needs. No API key, no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_site_breach_search
tools.description: Find breaches in the public breach catalog (which companies were breached, when, how many accounts, which data types). Filter by company name or domain, or omit `query` and sort to list e.g. the largest or newest breaches. Paginated; returns { total, page, items: [{ name, title, domain, breachDate, accounts, dataClasses, sources, url }] }. Catalog metadata only: to check whether a specific email, username or password was exposed use checkleaked_leak_check instead. No API key, no credits.

query.description: Company name or domain to match, e.g. linkedin or adobe.com. Omit to list the whole catalog in `sortBy` order

sortBy.description: Sort field: PwnCount = size, BreachDate = when it happened, AddedDate = when it was catalogued (default ModifiedDate)

lang.description: Language code (es, fr, de, …) for translated descriptions where cached

tools.name: checkleaked_site_breach
tools.description: Full public record of ONE catalogued breach by its exact catalog name (as returned by checkleaked_site_breach_search): breach and added dates, accounts affected, exposed data types, which databases list it (sources), verified flag, plain-text description and its page URL. Use after checkleaked_site_breach_search, or when a search result names a breach and you need its details. No API key, no credits.

name.description: Catalog name exactly as listed by checkleaked_site_breach_search, e.g. LinkedIn or Adobe

lang.description: Language code (es, fr, de, …) for a translated description

tools.name: checkleaked_site_latest_breach
tools.description: The single breach most recently added to the public catalog, in the same shape as checkleaked_site_breach. Use for "what is the newest breach?"; to list several recent ones use checkleaked_site_breach_search with sortBy=AddedDate. No API key, no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_site_briefing
tools.description: The latest CheckLeaked.cc daily cybersecurity briefing (security news, not breach data): date, title, summary, key takeaways, story titles and its page URL. Pass `lang` for a translated briefing. No API key, no credits.

lang.description: Language code (es, fr, de, …) for a translated briefing

tools.name: checkleaked_site_changelog
tools.description: Recent CheckLeaked.cc product changes, newest first: date, kind, area, title and a short body, plus the changelog page URL. Use for "what's new in CheckLeaked?"; it describes the service, not breaches (for newly catalogued breaches use checkleaked_site_latest_breach). No API key, no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_site_stats
tools.description: Two public CheckLeaked.cc counters: total searches served and total indexed breach records. Use for "how big is CheckLeaked?"; per-breach numbers come from checkleaked_site_breach. No API key, no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_site_pages
tools.description: Static list of CheckLeaked.cc web pages (search, pricing, FAQ, LeakRadar, Deep Search, developer API, bots, breach catalog, news, changelog, redeem, contact) with the URL and purpose of each. Use to send a user to the right page; it fetches nothing. No API key, no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_verify_auth
tools.description: Confirm the connected API key is accepted: returns { success: true }, or an Unauthorized error for a missing, wrong or revoked key. Use when a tool fails with an auth error. To also see which plan the key is on, use checkleaked_ping.

tools.name: checkleaked_ping
tools.description: Round-trip check that also names the key's plan: returns { plan, message: "Pong", time } (plan is free / plus / pro, with "(Unlock Role)" when an Unlock pass is active). Use at the start of a session to see what the account can search; limits per plan come from checkleaked_site_plans. No credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_leak_check
tools.description: Default breach search — start here. Looks a value up in the LeakCheck breach-dump index (merged with HIBP breach names) and returns every leaked record that contains it: { found, foundWithPass, results: [{ email, username, password, name, phone, ip, address, dob, sources: [{ Name, BreachDate }] }] }. Works for email, username, phone, domain (every account on it), keyword, password and hashes. Free plan: email and username only, with every field except email, username and sources masked; Plus adds phone and password searches, Pro every type, and both return plaintext (see checkleaked_site_plans). Uses one daily lookup only when something is found. For infostealer-captured credentials use checkleaked_leakradar_email_search; for name / street address / IP / VIN searches use checkleaked_dehashed.

check.description: Value to look up: an email, username, phone number, domain, keyword, password or hash

type.description: What `check` is. auto = detect (email, phone, hash or username); email; username; phone (digits); domain = every account on that email domain; origin = credentials leaked FROM that website; keyword = substring match; password = records using that password; hash = SHA-256 of an email (may be cut to 24 chars); phash = SHA-256 password hash. Legacy aliases: login = username, mass = keyword, pass_email / pass_login = password, domain_email = domain

tools.name: checkleaked_dehashed
tools.description: Second breach index (DeHashed), for fields checkleaked_leak_check cannot search: a person's full name, a street address, an IP address or a vehicle VIN, plus email / username / phone. Returns { entries: [{ email, username, password, hashed_password, name, address, phone, ip_address, obtained_from }], results, pages, page }. Live queries need Plus or Pro; other plans get previously stored results with passwords masked. Uses one daily lookup only when entries come back. Use it after checkleaked_leak_check to widen coverage, or first for name/address/IP/VIN.

entry.description: Value to search, 4-50 chars (e.g. a full name, a street address, an IP)

type.description: Field to match. free = send `entry` as a raw DeHashed query across all fields

page.description: Result page, 1-based (default 1); see `pages` in the response

tools.name: checkleaked_experimental
tools.description: Third breach index (Snusbase), useful for reverse lookups the other two do not offer: every account that used a given password or password hash, or that last logged in from an IP (lastip). Also searches email, username and name. Returns { found, foundWithPass, results: [{ email, username, password, hash, lastip, name, sources, line }] }. Any plan can call it; without Plus/Pro/Unlock the password, hash and line fields are masked. Uses one daily lookup only when fresh results are found. Start with checkleaked_leak_check; use this to cross-check or for password/hash/lastip pivots.

type.description: Field to match. mass = emails that START WITH `entry` (prefix wildcard); lastip = last login IP; hash = a password hash as stored in the breach

tools.name: checkleaked_crack_hash
tools.description: Turn a password hash back into its plaintext by looking it up in a table of hashes already cracked from breach data (no brute force). Takes hex hashes such as MD5, NTLM, SHA-1 or SHA-256. Returns { hash, plain } or a not_found error. Plus/Pro/Unlock; no lookup is spent. To check whether a known password is leaked use checkleaked_pwned_password instead.

hash.description: The hash, at least 32 characters (e.g. a 32-char MD5/NTLM or 40-char SHA-1 hex string)

tools.name: checkleaked_ip_lookup
tools.description: Geolocation and network owner of an IPv4/IPv6 address: country, region, city, coordinates, ISP, ASN, a reverse-geocoded address and WHOIS. Use to place an IP found in a breach record (e.g. a lastip). Not a breach search: to find accounts tied to an IP use checkleaked_dehashed (ip_address) or checkleaked_experimental (lastip). No credits.

ip.description: IP address to look up. If omitted, the address the request comes from is used (for a hosted AI app that is its server, not the end user)

tools.name: checkleaked_ghunt
tools.description: Google-account OSINT for one Gmail / Google Workspace address (GHunt): account id, name and profile picture, and which Google services (e.g. Maps reviews, Calendar) expose public data for it. Not a breach search; for leaks of the same address use checkleaked_leak_check. Plus/Pro/Unlock.

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_new
tools.description: Start monitoring an email, login (username) or domain: CheckLeaked re-checks it periodically and records a history snapshot whenever new breach results appear (delivered to the account's webhook if one is set, see checkleaked_webhook_set). Uses one of the plan's tracking slots; check free slots first with checkleaked_tracking_limits. For a one-off search use checkleaked_leak_check instead.

entry.description: Value to track: an email address, a login/username, or a domain

type.description: Type of entry: login (a username), email, or domain

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_delete
tools.description: Stop monitoring ONE tracked entry and free its slot. Pass its `email_unique_id` from checkleaked_tracking_entries (NOT the numeric `id` field). Its past snapshots stop updating. To clear saved search history instead, use checkleaked_tracking_clean.

email_unique_id.description: The entry's email_unique_id, as listed by checkleaked_tracking_entries

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_limits
tools.description: How many monitoring slots the account's plan allows and how many are in use: { limit, total }. Call before checkleaked_tracking_new to know whether a slot is free. No credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_entries
tools.description: List every entry the account is monitoring, with its value, type (email/login/domain) and email_unique_id (needed by checkleaked_tracking_delete). Use to find what is tracked before reading history with checkleaked_tracking_history. No credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_history
tools.description: Check history for one tracked entry: every snapshot with its date, found count and changes. Pass the same entry and type it was added with; use a snapshot's `id` with checkleaked_tracking_result for the full result.

entry.description: The tracked value (email, login or domain)

type.description: The type it was added with

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_result
tools.description: The full breach result stored in ONE monitoring snapshot (its `id` from checkleaked_tracking_history): the breach records found at that check. No credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_tracking_clean
tools.description: Clear the account's saved search history (the My Entries list on checkleaked.cc): every past search is unsaved and the IP address and user agent stored with it are erased. It does NOT stop monitoring anything; to stop tracking an entry use checkleaked_tracking_delete. Irreversible.

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search
tools.description: Raw stealer-log files, manual browsing step 1 of 3: find the file BLOCKS that contain `q` (or match the filters) and return their addresses (container_id + entry_path + seq), not parsed records. Then list a file's blocks with checkleaked_leakradar_raw_parts (step 2) and read one with checkleaked_leakradar_raw_part (step 3). If you just want the matching credentials/cookies, use checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search_lines instead (one call). Needs `q` or at least one filter. Plus/Pro; 1 credit per page that unlocks new blocks (repeat searches within 30 minutes are free).

q.description: Full-text query matched inside raw blocks

container_id.description: Restrict to a single container id

exts.description: File extensions to include (no leading dot)

categories.description: Raw file categories to include, e.g. ['stealer-logs']

file_name.description: Case-insensitive wildcards the entry name must match

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from a previous response for deep pagination

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_raw_parts
tools.description: Raw stealer-log files, manual browsing step 2 of 3: list the sequential blocks (seq numbers) of ONE file found by checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search, so you can page through a large file and pick which block to read with checkleaked_leakradar_raw_part. Returns block metadata only, no leaked content, no credits.

container_id.description: Container id from a raw search result

entry_path.description: Entry path from a raw search result

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_raw_part
tools.description: Raw stealer-log files, manual browsing step 3 of 3: read the text of ONE block (container_id + entry_path + seq from checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search or checkleaked_leakradar_raw_parts). Locked blocks come back redacted (censored=true, █); auto_unlock=true (default) returns the plaintext and spends a credit. For search-and-extract in one call use checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search_lines.

trim_overlap.description: Strip the overlap prefix carried over from the previous block

auto_unlock.description: Unlock and return plaintext (default true, costs a credit). Set false to get the redacted block.

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search_lines
tools.description: Raw stealer-log files, one-call extraction (preferred): search the raw files for `q`, unlock the matching blocks and return only the parsed records that match (credential lines, cookies, autofill rows). Use this first when investigating raw stealer logs; fall back to the 3-step checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search -> raw_parts -> raw_part flow only to read a whole file. For structured credential rows (url, username, password) by email or username use checkleaked_leakradar_email_search instead. Plus/Pro; 1 credit per call.

q.description: Full-text query matched inside raw blocks. Required.

max_hits.description: Blocks to unlock and parse (default 100). Each costs an upstream fetch.

categories.description: Raw file categories to include, e.g. ['stealer-logs']

file_name.description: Case-insensitive wildcards the entry name must match

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_email_search
tools.description: LeakRadar stealer-log credential index, lookup by ONE email address or username: returns the credential rows captured by infostealer malware (site URL, login, password, date) for that identity. Use for "which sites' passwords were stolen for this person?". For breach-database dumps (company breaches) use checkleaked_leak_check instead; to filter by site, password or domain use checkleaked_leakradar_advanced_search. Returns { items: [{ id, url, username, password, password_strength, added_at }], total, page }. Available on every plan; rows always come back unlocked, 1 credit per page that unlocks new rows (repeats within 30 minutes are free).

email.description: The email address or username to look up

is_email.description: true = match it only as an email, false = only as a username, omit = both

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_advanced_search
tools.description: LeakRadar stealer-log credential index, filtered search: combine facets instead of one identity, e.g. every credential captured for a site (url_domain / url_host), usernames or passwords containing a string, a password-strength class or an indexed-date window. Each field takes an array (OR by default, force_and=true for AND). Rows come back unlocked: { items: [{ id, url, username, password, password_strength, added_at }], total }. For a single email or username use checkleaked_leakradar_email_search; for a company-wide count only use checkleaked_leakradar_domain_summary. Plus/Pro; 1 credit per page that unlocks new rows.

added_from.description: Only leaks indexed on/after this ISO datetime

added_to.description: Only leaks indexed on/before this ISO datetime

force_and.description: Require all values within each field (AND)

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_domain_summary
tools.description: Exposure report for ONE company domain from the LeakRadar stealer-log index: how many employees (logins on @domain), customers (logins to the domain's sites) and third parties are compromised, without returning the credentials themselves. Use for "how exposed is example.com?"; to see the actual rows for its sites use checkleaked_leakradar_advanced_search with url_domain. light=true returns only the headline counts. Every plan (free accounts have a small daily cap); no credits.

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_dark_web_search
tools.description: Search posts scraped from dark-web forums and markets (titles, post text, authors), e.g. sale threads that mention a company or a database. Returns posts, not credentials: for leaked logins use checkleaked_leak_check or checkleaked_leakradar_email_search. Use `query` for a simple search, or title/content/author for field filters. Plus/Pro.

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_pwned
tools.description: Count how often a password appears in the LeakRadar STEALER-LOG corpus (passwords captured by infostealer malware), with k-anonymity: the SHA-1 is computed inside this MCP process and only its first 5 hex chars are sent. Returns { pwned, count, prefix }. The public HIBP Pwned Passwords set is checked by checkleaked_pwned_password instead (free); to turn a hash back into a password use checkleaked_crack_hash.

password.description: Password to check (hashed locally, never sent)

sha1.description: Its SHA-1 as 40 hex chars, instead of the password (only the first 5 are sent)

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_unlock
tools.description: Reveal specific LeakRadar leak rows by id when they reached you masked (for example ids saved from the checkleaked.cc LeakRadar pages). The LeakRadar searches in this server already return unlocked rows, so you rarely need it. Charged 1 credit per row newly unlocked; rows already unlocked on the account are free. Pro plan.

target_list_id.description: Optional list id to assign the unlocked items to

tools.name: checkleaked_leakradar_task_status
tools.description: Status of a LeakRadar background task (an asynchronous unlock or export started on the account) by its task id. Poll until it reports completed (running=false), then repeat the search to read the unlocked rows. No credits.

id.description: Task id returned by an async endpoint

tools.name: checkleaked_domain_whois
tools.description: WHOIS registration record of a domain: registrar, creation and expiry dates, name servers, status and registrant fields where published. Returns { domain, found, whois }. Use to date or attribute a domain; it is not a breach search (for accounts on a domain use checkleaked_leak_check with type=domain, for its exposure use checkleaked_leakradar_domain_summary). No credits.

domain.description: Domain to look up, e.g. example.com

tools.name: checkleaked_pwned_password
tools.description: Check whether a password is in the public HIBP Pwned Passwords list (passwords exposed in data breaches) WITHOUT sending it: the SHA-1 is computed inside the MCP process, only its first 5 hex chars are sent and the suffix is matched locally. Returns { pwned, count, prefix }. The default password check: no credits, every plan; the password and its full hash never appear in the output. For passwords captured by infostealer malware use checkleaked_leakradar_pwned; to find which accounts used a password use checkleaked_leak_check (type=password).

password.description: Password to check (never leaves this process)

tools.name: checkleaked_email_breach_kanon
tools.description: Privacy-first yes/no for an email address WITHOUT sending it: SHA-256 of the lowercased, trimmed email is computed inside the MCP process and only its first 24 hex chars are sent. Returns { found, sources[], fields[] }: which breaches contain it and which data types leaked, but no records or passwords. Use when the user does not want the address itself sent, or as a free first check; for the actual leaked records use checkleaked_leak_check. No credits; the email is never echoed.

email.description: Email address to check (hashed locally, never sent)

tools.name: checkleaked_name_insight
tools.description: Likely gender, cultural origin and meaning of a personal name (offline name dictionary plus Wikidata/Wikipedia), e.g. to interpret a name field from a breach record. Not a people search: it says nothing about a specific person. No credits.

name.description: Given name or full name, e.g. 'Joan Sztejnberg'

tools.name: checkleaked_webhook_get
tools.description: Show the account's tracking webhook — url, enabled, secret_hint (last 4 chars), fail_count, last_status / last_error / last_attempt / last_success — or null when none is configured. The secret itself is never returned here; only checkleaked_webhook_set returns it, on create or rotate. Destination: HTTPS only, on a public host (no private/loopback IPs, no localhost). Events: `tracking.finding` — one JSON POST per tracking finding. Every delivery carries `X-CheckLeaked-Event`, `X-CheckLeaked-Delivery` (uuid) and `X-CheckLeaked-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>`; verify by recomputing the HMAC over `<t>.<raw body>` with the stored secret and comparing constant-time (Node example in resource checkleaked://webhooks). Retries at 2s and 8s on network error / 5xx / 429; auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures. Formats: a Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams or Google Chat webhook URL gets the finding rendered natively for that service (format auto-detected); any other URL gets the generic signed JSON event.

tools.name: checkleaked_webhook_set
tools.description: Create or update the account's tracking webhook. The response carries the plaintext `secret` ONLY when the webhook is created or rotate_secret=true — store it then, it cannot be read back later. Destination: HTTPS only, on a public host (no private/loopback IPs, no localhost). Events: `tracking.finding` — one JSON POST per tracking finding. Every delivery carries `X-CheckLeaked-Event`, `X-CheckLeaked-Delivery` (uuid) and `X-CheckLeaked-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>`; verify by recomputing the HMAC over `<t>.<raw body>` with the stored secret and comparing constant-time (Node example in resource checkleaked://webhooks). Retries at 2s and 8s on network error / 5xx / 429; auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures. Formats: a Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams or Google Chat webhook URL gets the finding rendered natively for that service (format auto-detected); any other URL gets the generic signed JSON event.

url.description: HTTPS destination URL on a public host

rotate_secret.description: Issue a new signing secret (returned once, in this response)

format.description: Delivery shape: json = generic signed event (Zapier, Make, n8n, SIEM); slack = Block Kit for a Slack Incoming Webhook (Mattermost/Rocket.Chat compatible); discord = webhook embed; teams = Adaptive Card for a Microsoft Teams Workflows webhook; google_chat = cardsV2 message. auto (default) detects the service from the URL host on create and whenever the URL changes.

tools.name: checkleaked_webhook_test
tools.description: Send one signed test `tracking.finding` event (payload test=true) to the configured webhook, no retries. Returns { delivered, status, error, duration_ms }. Limited to 5 per minute. Destination: HTTPS only, on a public host (no private/loopback IPs, no localhost). Events: `tracking.finding` — one JSON POST per tracking finding. Every delivery carries `X-CheckLeaked-Event`, `X-CheckLeaked-Delivery` (uuid) and `X-CheckLeaked-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>`; verify by recomputing the HMAC over `<t>.<raw body>` with the stored secret and comparing constant-time (Node example in resource checkleaked://webhooks). Retries at 2s and 8s on network error / 5xx / 429; auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures. Formats: a Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams or Google Chat webhook URL gets the finding rendered natively for that service (format auto-detected); any other URL gets the generic signed JSON event.

tools.name: checkleaked_webhook_delete
tools.description: Delete the account's tracking webhook: stops all deliveries and discards the secret.

tools.name: checkleaked_private_bots_get
tools.description: List the account's private Discord / Telegram bots — per platform: state (stopped / starting / online / error), enabled, bot_username, bot_id, token_hint (last 4 chars), last_error, last_started and invite_url (Discord) — plus plan_ok (Pro / Plus required), configured (server-side token key present) and max_per_platform (1). Private bots are Pro/Plus only. Bring your own bot token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot → Reset Token) or Telegram @BotFather (/newbot). The token is validated against Discord (`users/@me`) / Telegram (`getMe`), stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and NEVER returned — only its last 4 chars (`token_hint`) plus the validated `bot_username` / `bot_id`. The bot runs on CheckLeaked's servers with the same commands as the shared CheckLeaked bots and answers ONLY the owner's linked account (anyone else gets "This private bot answers only the account that runs it."), so nobody else can spend the owner's credits. One bot per platform per account; a lapsed plan stops the bot. Discord bots need no privileged intents (slash commands and DMs work; prefix commands in servers cannot read message content) — the response's `invite_url` adds the bot to a server.

tools.name: checkleaked_private_bot_set
tools.description: Create, replace or pause/resume the account's private bot on one platform. Pass `token` to (re)store a token — validated first, saved encrypted, never echoed back. Pass `enabled` alone (no token) to pause (false) or resume (true) an existing bot. Returns { bot } with state, bot_username, token_hint and invite_url; errors: plan not Pro/Plus, private bots not configured on the server, or the token-validation reason. Private bots are Pro/Plus only. Bring your own bot token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot → Reset Token) or Telegram @BotFather (/newbot). The token is validated against Discord (`users/@me`) / Telegram (`getMe`), stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and NEVER returned — only its last 4 chars (`token_hint`) plus the validated `bot_username` / `bot_id`. The bot runs on CheckLeaked's servers with the same commands as the shared CheckLeaked bots and answers ONLY the owner's linked account (anyone else gets "This private bot answers only the account that runs it."), so nobody else can spend the owner's credits. One bot per platform per account; a lapsed plan stops the bot. Discord bots need no privileged intents (slash commands and DMs work; prefix commands in servers cannot read message content) — the response's `invite_url` adds the bot to a server.

token.description: Bot token from the Discord Developer Portal or @BotFather (validated, stored encrypted, never returned)

enabled.description: Pause (false) / resume (true) the bot; alone it toggles without touching the token

tools.name: checkleaked_private_bot_delete
tools.description: Remove the account's private bot on one platform: stops it and discards the encrypted token. Returns { removed: true }.
